newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai plan seen negative for bank, finance shares.
newsitem.headline: Thai plan seen negative for bank, finance shares.

text.p: Premiums fetched by Thai bank and finance shares on the foreign board over the main board should fall if a central bank plan to raise foreign ownership limits of financial institutions takes off, analysts said on Tuesday.

"In the short-term, there will be heavy selling of bank and finance shares in the foreign board due to an increased supply of the shares for foreign investors to buy," Thanawat Patchimkul banking analyst at Seamico Securities, told Reuters
"This will narrow the premium of these shares between the foreign and local boards."

Bank of Thailand governor Rerngchai Marakanond said late on Monday the central bank was considering easing the foreign holding limit in banks and finance companies. The move was aimed at attracting more investment from foreigners into Thai financial markets, he said.
Foreigners are at present allowed to hold no more than a 25 percent stake in local bank and finance companies.
Rerngchai said a new limit was being worked out by the central bank, and the announcement sparked selling of major finance and bank shares on the foreign board on Tuesday.
Donaldson Hartman, a banking analyst at Salomon Brothers, said additional falls in bank and finance shares on the foreign board were likely and that would also affect main board prices.
"In the past, foreign share prices have determined the direction of the market. In other words, they have also pushed the local prices down," Hartman said.

Share prices of three major banks -- Bangkok Bank Plc, Thai Farmers Bank Plc and Siam Commercial Bank Plc -- would be the most affected due to the relatively high premiums between their shares on the foreign and main boards.

At midday on Tuesday, Thai Farmers dropped eight baht to 161 on the foreign board, compared to a three-baht fall to 119 on the main board. Bangkok Bank was down eight to 238 on the foreign board and down two to 183 baht on the main board.
Siam Commercial Bank dropped 13 to 178 on the foreign board compared to a three-baht drop to 167 on the local board.
Analysts said in the long term, an increase in foreign holdings would help reduce volatility in banking and finance shares, as most investments by foreign institutions were long term.
"Foreign investors normally have a long-term investment strategy. The increased foreign ownership will reduce the volatility in bank and finance share prices," Thanawat at Seamico Securities said.
He added that increased shareholdings by some foreign financial institutions would also enable some technological transfer and network expansion for local financial institutions.
